samples.summary: `seg()` makes the synchronous `fileUrl()` throwable, and it is called during React render with no ErrorBoundary anywhere in the frontend
samples.evidence: `fileUrl(documentId, token)` is evaluated in the body of `PdfCollabProvider` (packages/frontend/src/app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:139) while building its context value; `documentId` is a route param (`packages/frontend/src/app/files/file-detail.tsx:209` passes `id!` from the router). Every other `seg()` call site added by this diff sits inside an `async` API function, so the throw surfaces as a rejected promise a query can render as an error state — this one throws synchronously during render. A grep for `ErrorBoundary|errorElement` across `packages/frontend/src` returns nothing, so an id of `.`/`..` (reachable as `/f/%2E%2E`, which the browser does not normalize and react-router percent-decodes into the param) unmounts the whole tree instead of showing a not-found state. Other sync call sites with the same shape: `packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:726`. Fix belongs on the new code — either keep `fileUrl` total (encode without throwing) or guard the id where it enters the route.

samples.summary: The new image-host guard uses exact origin equality against `--server`, but the frontend persists ABSOLUTE image URLs into document content, so existing docs can stop exporting on any self-hosted/dev origin mismatch
samples.evidence: `resolveImageUrl` in packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-upload.ts:127-129 rewrites every backend image URL to absolute before it is written into the CRDT ("EVERY path that writes a backend image URL into a CRDT document has to apply this"), so stored `src` values are e.g. `http://localhost:3000/images/...` in dev and whatever `VITE_BACKEND_API_URL` is in a self-hosted install. `assertFetchableImageUrl` exempts such a URL only via `sameOriginAsServer` (string origin equality) or `WAFFLEBASE_IMAGE_HOSTS`. Any alias mismatch between the browser's API origin and the CLI's configured `server` — `localhost` vs `127.0.0.1`, http vs https, a second port, or a private-IP API host reached under a different name — now makes the previously-working `docs export` (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:261) and `slides export` (packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:209) fail with "non-public address" for documents that used to embed fine. Consumers of `createImageFetcher` outside the diff inherit this without change.

samples.summary: `login` is the one backend-talking command left throwing a hand-built `HTTP <status>` error, contradicting the "every command reports HTTP_ERROR" contract this change advertises
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:62, :79 and :96 still do `if (!res.ok) throw new Error("... (HTTP ${wsRes.status}) ...")`, which `outputError` reports as `{code: "ERROR"}`. packages/cli/README.md:137-140 and docs/design/cli.md:1084-1086 (both already updated on this branch) state that HTTP_ERROR is "a single classifier for every command, so the code an agent branches on never depends on which subcommand it ran". An agent branching on `HTTP_ERROR` gets `ERROR` from `wafflebase login`.

A grep for `ErrorBoundary|errorElement` across `packages/frontend/src` returns nothing, so an id of `.`/`..` (reachable as `/f/%2E%2E`, which the browser does not normalize and react-router percent-decodes into the param) unmounts the whole tree instead of showing a not-found state. verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out in the repo. `seg()` throws for "."/".." (packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts:18-23) and is called from the synchronous `fileUrl()` (packages/frontend/src/api/files.ts:22-25). `fileUrl(documentId, token)` is evaluated in the render body of the PDF collab provider while building the context value (packages/frontend/src/app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:139), with `documentId` originating as the raw `/f/:id` router param (App.tsx:127 -> file-detail.tsx:172, passed as `id!` at file-detail.tsx:228). A second synchronous render-time call site exists at packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:726. A grep for ErrorBoundary|errorElement|componentDidCatch|getDerivedStateFromError across packages/frontend/src returns no matches, so a render-time throw unmounts the tree rather than showing an error state. I examined the strongest already-guarded candidate: file-detail.tsx:204 redirects when `docError || !documentData`, and `fetchDocument` is async (api/documents.ts:45-47) so a bad id rejects there first. That closes the cold-load path but not all paths: the same query sets `placeholderData: keepPreviousData` (file-detail.tsx:195), so on a client-side navigation from a valid pdf document to a bad id the placeholder keeps `documentData` populated and `docError` false for at least one render, mounting PdfFileLayout with the unvalidated id and hitting the throwing `fileUrl` at pdf-collab.tsx:139. Client-side navigations to `/f/${id}` exist (image-viewer.tsx:103, document-list-utils.ts:162). Since I cannot show that path is unreachable, the guard is not sufficient and the finding stands.

finding.evidence: `resolveImageUrl` in packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-upload.ts:127-129 rewrites every backend image URL to absolute before it is written into the CRDT ("EVERY path that writes a backend image URL into a CRDT document has to apply this"), so stored `src` values are e.g. `http://localhost:3000/images/...` in dev and whatever `VITE_BACKEND_API_URL` is in a self-hosted install. `assertFetchableImageUrl` exempts such a URL only via `sameOriginAsServer` (string origin equality) or `WAFFLEBASE_IMAGE_HOSTS`. Any alias mismatch between the browser's API origin and the CLI's configured `server` — `localhost` vs `127.0.0.1`, http vs https, a second port, or a private-IP API host reached under a different name — now makes the previously-working `docs export` (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:261) and `slides export` (packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:209) fail with "non-public address" for documents that used to embed fine. Consumers of `createImageFetcher` outside the diff inherit this without change.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repo. (1) The frontend does persist ABSOLUTE image URLs into document content: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-upload.ts:127-131 prefixes VITE_BACKEND_API_URL and uploadImageFile returns that at :58, consumed by slides-detail.tsx:313/655, board-image.ts:12, sheet-view.tsx:504, miro-import-runner.ts:164; the docs pipeline does the same via export-utils.ts:12-18,39 -> image-insert.ts:11-14,61-63. (2) The CLI guard exempts such URLs only by literal origin string equality (image-fetcher.ts:122-128) or WAFFLEBASE_IMAGE_HOSTS (134-139), otherwise isPrivateHost (67-102) makes assertFetchableImageUrl throw "non-public address" (184-191). So a localhost/127.0.0.1, http/https, port, or private-IP-vs-hostname mismatch between the browser's API origin and the CLI's --server turns previously-exporting documents into hard failures. (3) The consumers outside the diff are real and pass no allowedHosts: packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:261-263 and packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:209, both using getConfig(opts).server (config.ts:88-158), which is under no constraint to string-match VITE_BACKEND_API_URL. No refutation ground holds: the code is as described (not not-present); WAFFLEBASE_IMAGE_HOSTS is an opt-in operator escape hatch requiring manual action, not a guard rendering the break unreachable (not already-guarded); and a stricter new precondition breaking data written by another package, discoverable only by grepping outside the diff, is squarely in the blast-radius lane (not out-of-scope). Major impact: existing exports regress.

finding.summary: New frontend `seg()` id-pinning guard is bypassed by every other browser API module that interpolates the same route-param ids
finding.evidence: The change introduces `packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts` and applies `seg()` only inside `packages/frontend/src/api/documents.ts`. The same document/workspace/folder ids (which reach these modules from the URL bar and pasted links, exactly the source the new doc comment cites) are still interpolated raw into session-carrying `fetchWithAuth` calls elsewhere: `packages/frontend/src/api/share-links.ts:60` and `:78` (`/documents/${documentId}/share-links`), `:89` (`/share-links/${id}`); `packages/frontend/src/api/files.ts:22` (`/documents/${documentId}/file`); `packages/frontend/src/api/analytics.ts:127` (`/documents/${documentId}/analytics`); `packages/frontend/src/api/folders.ts:42,64,82`; `packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:48,75,88,184,196,212` (incl. `/${workspaceId}/api-keys/${keyId}`); `packages/frontend/src/api/datasources.ts:45,65,78,90,104`. A `..`-bearing id reaching any of these walks the request off the intended endpoint with the user's session attached — the precise condition the new guard exists to stop. Fix belongs at these call sites (add `seg()`), not in the new module.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the new `seg()` guard is applied only in `documents.ts` and that other frontend API modules still interpolate route-param ids raw into `fetchWithAuth` URLs. Reading the cited files shows the opposite: every cited site already imports and applies `seg()`. `share-links.ts` imports `seg` (line 3) and wraps all ids (`:61`, `:79`, `:90`, plus `:103`); `files.ts:23` uses `seg(documentId)`; `analytics.ts:128` uses `seg(documentId)`; `folders.ts:11,25,43,65,83` all use `seg()`; `workspaces.ts:49,76,89,103,116,131,144,185,197,213,228,273,292,305,317,340` all use `seg()`, including `/${seg(workspaceId)}/api-keys/${seg(keyId)}` at :213; `datasources.ts:46,66,79,91,105` all use `seg(id)`; `miro.ts:94` uses `seg(workspaceId)`. A repo-wide grep for `${...id...}` under `packages/frontend/src/api` surfaced no unwrapped route-segment interpolation — the only bare ones are query-string values already passed through `encodeURIComponent` (`workspaces.ts:227`, `files.ts:24`), which are not path segments. `notifications.ts` composes URLs from a `base()` helper with no interpolated ids. The bypassing sites the finding names do not exist as described, so there is nothing to fix.

finding.summary: New `assertFetchableImageUrl` host guard can break existing `docs export` / `slides export` runs against self-hosted or split-origin deployments
finding.evidence: `createImageFetcher` is consumed by `packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:261` and `packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:209`, both passing only `getConfig(opts).server` as the exemption origin. Any image `src` that is an absolute URL on an origin other than the configured `--server` and resolves to a private/loopback address is now a hard failure of the whole export: self-hosted installs where blobs/images are served by a separate internal host or port (e.g. MinIO/S3 at `http://10.0.0.5:9000`, a reverse proxy on a second port), and the common `--server http://localhost:3000` vs stored `http://127.0.0.1:3000/...` spelling mismatch (different origins, so `sameOriginAsServer` fails and `isPrivateHost` refuses). Previously these fetched fine. Backend-generated URLs are relative (`packages/backend/src/api/v1/images.controller.ts:74`) so the default path is safe, but documents imported/edited with absolute srcs are not.

verdict.reason: The guard is present and reachable exactly as described. packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:164-192 throws for any http(s) image src whose host is a literal private/loopback/link-local/CGNAT address unless it is same-origin with `serverBase` (line 184) or listed in `allowedHosts` (line 185). Both consumers — packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:261-263 and packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:209 — pass only `serverBase: getConfig(opts).server`, so the sole exemption existing installs get is the configured server's exact origin; the WAFFLEBASE_IMAGE_HOSTS fallback (image-fetcher.ts:208-209) is new operator config no current deployment sets, so it does not make the break unreachable (`already-guarded` does not apply). The reviewer's mitigating claim (backend URLs are relative, images.controller.ts:74) is true at the controller but understates exposure: the frontend deliberately persists ABSOLUTE image URLs into documents via resolveImageUrl (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-upload.ts:127-131, used at :58 with a comment at :122-125 saying every write path must do this; also packages/frontend/src/app/docs/export-utils.ts:12-18, :39), built from VITE_BACKEND_API_URL which is documented as http://localhost:3000 in dev. So stored absolute srcs on a private/loopback origin are the normal case, and any origin/spelling divergence from `--server` (localhost vs 127.0.0.1, second port, split MinIO/blob host) now hard-fails the entire export where it previously fetched. This is a behaviour change to an exported symbol plus a new required config that existing call sites do not supply — squarely in the blast-radius lane, not merely a judgement on the guard's security design. Nothing in the repo makes it not-present, unreachable, or out-of-scope.
